facts.PRODUCT-AND-TOOL-NAMES: The tool is Codkit; a consumer product and its fork-specific namespace are external inputs.
facts.INTERVENTION-ID-FORMAT: Intervention ids use `CK-<area>-<number>` and are unique within a patch set.
facts.OWN-DIRECTORY-CONFIGURED: The downstream-owned source directory below `src/vs/` is configured per patch set and has no product-specific default.

facts.TERM-UPSTREAM: Upstream is the VS Code history consumed by a managed fork; a pin is an exact tag and commit.
facts.TERM-PATCH-SET: A patch set is the complete machine-readable downstream delta plus its configuration, state, and inventory.
facts.TERM-FORK-TREE: A managed fork tree is the reproducible checkout to which Codkit applies a patch set.
facts.TERM-INTERVENTION: An intervention is one attributable downstream change represented by a Codkit layer.

facts.SPEC-LANGUAGE-IS-ENGLISH: The specifications of this repository - `vibevm/vibespecs/common/*` and `vibevm/vibespecs/modules/codkit/*` - are written in English: prose, decision records, acceptance scenarios, status comments and section titles alike. Identifiers, anchors, file names, command names, flags, settings, keys, error codes and code stay as they are, and a quotation from upstream, from a log or from a user-facing string keeps the language of its source. Commit messages are English as well (the attribution policy and Conventional Commits). A consumer product keeps its own rule for its own specifications and is not bound by this one. Owner ruling of 2026-09-08; the earlier Russian text of the module specifications was translated under it.

facts.DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0: **1.0.0 is the development version.** Every package this repository ships - the standards package, the agent-skills package and the runtime library - carries version 1.0.0 and is changed in place under that number: a product takes the changed copy with `codkit standards load --upgrade` and `codkit runtime load --upgrade`, and no change bumps the number. This is how the internal packages of the package manager live during development (30 of the 31 installed here are at 1.0.0), and the owner applied the same rule to this tool and to the product on 2026-09-08. Honest re-releases - a new number for every change - return only when the owner says so explicitly; `EDITION-IS-MUTABLE-FOR-NOW` in the standards protocol and `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION` in PROP-014 say the same for the standards edition. A version directory named after an older number is a tombstone: its content moves to `v1.0.0`, and the anchors that carried the old number stay as tombstones pointing at the new ones.

p.PATCHSET-HISTORY-IMMUTABLE: Published patch-set history is not rewritten; generated fork refs are derived and replaceable under their guarded workflow.

p.CURRENT-TREE-ZERO-RETIRED-NAME: The current checked-out Codkit tree has zero occurrences of the retired consumer-product identifier in tracked paths or tracked content. Preserved Git object history is intentionally outside this current-tree gate.
